correctness.rationale: Pass for the complete repaired RESULT.md. The frozen appeal to a two-sided generating-functional neighborhood is not valid under only a finite order-j moment: probabilities proportional to k^(−j−2) give finite m_j but infinite E[(1+c)^K] for every c>0. The repair works on the nonpositive generating-function cube and bounds each order-k derivative by m_k exp(−kδt) times the product of the test-function suprema. The representation therefore holds as a mixed factorial cumulant under exactly the stated moment assumption. The integrated cumulant mass is bm_j/(jδ), so the possible joint-origin singularity is locally integrable. The Bessel formula yields uniform far-field asymptotics since S/R² ranges over compact positive intervals. The ratio exponent is minus α times the exact deficit j Σ(r_i−r̄)²/(√(j Σr_i²)+Σr_i), with denominator asymptotic to 2jR in the shell. This proves the zero set, the Gaussian ratio and the strict trichotomy without assuming separated coordinates or dropping a prefactor. The eigen-direction with constant radial offsets has no transverse deficit, and order-one density is everywhere positive. The private repair clarifies the valid range of fixed nonzero vectors, including individual zero coordinates away from the joint origin. The finite checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This normalization asks whether particles far from the source co-occur more strongly when one burst age can explain all distances. The answer distinguishes exponential suppression from a power-law ridge and gives a precise scale and profile usable for comparing configurations at large common radius. Neither the standard radial kernel nor a fixed-ray rate alone answers that comparison, and the conclusion is explicitly about connected factorial cumulant densities, not detection in a realization.
